  `Mutex<WebmWriter>`. It writes the bytes it is handed and never decodes.
- `graphic_package.rs` · `ffi_graphic_package.rs` — the `.fjgraphic` package
  (spec §11 G-46): the package request's checks, the in-package name
  legaliser (legal names claimed first, G-23 (c)'s suffixes on a clash),
  `manifest.json`, the stored zip and its CRC-32, and the write (`.partial`
  renamed into place); names no `graphic` item. `graphic_package_read.rs`
  is the reader (G-47): stored entries only, `manifest.json` first,
  `"fjgraphic": 1` (a newer version refused by number), each file's size and
  SHA-256 against the manifest, no path out of `fonts/`/`assets/`; it
  answers the checked manifest and each file's offset. `ffi_graphic_package.rs`
  is `rc_graphic_package_write`, answering the manifest it wrote, and
  `rc_graphic_package_read`.
- `hdr10.rs` · `ffi_hdr10.rs` — an HDR10 file's peak (spec §11 HD-6,
  HD-12): the mastering-display and content-light blobs of a sample
  description, else the first sample's prefix SEI (payloads 137, 144,
  emulation-prevention bytes removed); MaxCLL first, rounded in u64,
  clamped to 10,000; `rc_hdr10_peak` its export. `av1_peak` the same for
  AV1 (HD-18): the HDR_CLL and HDR_MDCV metadata OBUs of the `av1C`'s
  config OBUs, else the first sample, luminance in 24.8 fixed point;
  `rc_hdr10_av1_peak` its export. Pure, bounded reads. `rc_hdr10_still_peak`
  (HD-20) is the third export, over `hdr10_still.rs`.
- `hdr10_still.rs` — a PQ still's HDR10 peak (spec §11 HD-20, #325): a PNG's
  `cLLI`/`mDCV` chunks before the first IDAT, else a HEIF/AVIF primary item's
  `clli`/`mdcv` properties (its first `ipma`); MaxCLL first, the same rounding
  and clamp as `hdr10.rs`. Pure, every index checked against the buffer.
- `model_matte.rs` — the matte vocabulary (format version 14, spec §11 MT-1):
  `TrackMatte` (`none`, `alpha`, `alpha_inverted`, `luma`, `luma_inverted`)
  and `is_none`, re-exported through `model_props.rs`; the FIELD
  `Track.matte` stays in `model_track.rs`, skipped when `none` (an ordinary
  track writes no key), as `ColorAdjust`'s nine tone keys are when 0.
- `model_color.rs` — `normalise_color`, G-12's colour grammar (hex,
  `rgb()`/`rgba()`, `hsl()`/`hsla()` and the CSS named colours, from
  svgtypes' table) to lowercase `#rrggbb[aa]`; out of range is refused,
  never clamped. The stdlib's `__parseColour` implements the same grammar,
  and both suites read `graphic/tests/colours.json`. `rc_normalise_color`
  (`ffi.rs`) exports it for the Inspector's colour defaults (spec §11 G-25
  (c)), and `model_graphic.rs`'s `check_schema` refuses a `color` default
  it refuses (G-25 (a)). `color_channels` and `color_hex` (which
  `normalise_color` writes through) and `oklab_mix` are
  `actions_graphic.rs`'s blend's: `oklab_mix` is the stdlib's
  `interpolateColors` ported operation for operation (spec §11 G-40), now
  bytes/255 through `oklab_mix_unit` and ×255 rounded out; `oklab_mix_unit`
  and `oklab_mix_rgb` (0–1 floats, clamped, never rounded) are
  `actions_color.rs`'s (G-43). Three suites read `graphic/tests/oklab.json`:
  the stdlib's, `graphic_actions.rs` and `action_colours.rs`.
- `model_query.rs` — reading a project: `Project::new`, id allocation, the
  `clip`/`track`/`media`/`marker`/`nest` lookups, `clips_on`, `duration`,
  `validate` with its nesting walk, and `source_size`; and the shared
  spellings of a fresh thing: `Track::ordinary` (every flag off),
  `Source::media` (the media a source reads, exhaustive over the kinds),
  `next_track_name` ("Track N" by the count), `numbered_track` (allocated
  and named, not inserted) and `remint` (a copied clip's fresh ids: the
  clip's, then each action's). The three source-window measurements moved
  out to `source_window.rs`.
- `frame_grid.rs` — clip-time normalization shared by canvas rate changes,
  both full-paste paths and unnest. It snaps placement start, delegates the
  source-bounded duration to `source_window.rs`, clamps action spans, snaps
  present base motion/text timing through the patch snappers, and snaps a
  graphic's `in` and `length` through `recipe_graphic.rs`'s
  `graphic_resnapped` (spec §11 G-18). It does not change source positions,
  action-end payloads or audio envelopes. On a ramped clip (SR-19 (g))
  `resnap_actions` snaps the speed actions without clamping them into the
  clip (clamping would change what it reads), and `resnap_clip_times` holds
  the duration a second time over the snapped map.
- `source_window.rs` — THE source window: how much material a clip shows,
  how much lies either side of it, and the one way a source in point moves.
  `content_length_in_source` reads `speed_map.rs`'s map for a ramped clip
  (SR-10), so the one function still says how much source any clip reads.
  On a ramped clip (SR-18) the tail readers go through `time_for_source`,
  `in` moves by `source_read_by` / `source_advanced_through` (trims, roll,
  split, freeze), `front_edge_held` bisects the front edge to a frame that
  fits, and `window_of` / `overrun` (moved here from `edit_action_speed.rs`)
  are the fit test.
  **Every name here carries its UNIT**, because the readers divide by a
  clip's speed where the movers multiply by it: `content_length_in_source`,
  `last_in_point` and `last_still_time` answer in SOURCE ticks;
  `source_head_on_timeline`, `source_length_on_timeline` and
  `longest_duration_on_grid` — the bound, snapped DOWN (spec §11, #22) — in
  TIMELINE ticks. **Every site that WRITES a media clip's window reads the
  bound here, and which function it reads says what it writes** (spec §11,
  D4-2 to D4-5): `longest_duration_on_grid_of` is the bound from the pieces,
  with the clip's `start` among them, because a DURATION is measured from 0
  and an END from the clip's own start and the two are not the same number;
  `latest_end_on_grid` and `earliest_start_on_grid` are the timeline
  POSITIONS `trim_end` / `roll` and `trim_start` / `roll` /
  `head_handle_frames` clamp to (positions, so not a `SourceBound`);
  `duration_resnapped` is what every RE-SNAP of a media duration writes
  (`resnap`, `paste` twice, `unnest`, `relink_media`'s hold to a shorter file)
  and `duration_at_speed` what
  `set_speed` writes. No local clamp anywhere else. A measurement is a
  `SourceBound` and not an `Option`,
  because `None` meant "unbounded, apply no clamp" to a trim and "no handle
  at all" to a transition: the three arms are `Unbounded` (a source with no
  window), `Unmeasured` (a media window that exists and cannot be measured)
  and `Timeline`, and a caller picks what `Unmeasured` means to it BY NAME,
  `or_unbounded` or `or_empty`. `in_advanced` / `source_advanced` is the one
  `round(Δ × speed)` mover the six placement sites used to write out. Cut
  out of `model_query.rs` by road map 7 §10's phase A.
- `time.rs` — `Ticks`, `TIMESCALE`, `Fps`, frame snapping, timecode
  format/parse (non-drop `HH:MM:SS:FF` and `HH:MM:SS.mmm`). Snapping keeps
  frame indices wide through directional adjustment and saturates only at the
  public tick/index result. `frames_in` (whole grid frames in a length),
  `frames_back` (the grid position k frames before the frame nearest a
  position) and `frames_within` (the most whole frames back from a position
  that stay within a span), `frames_between` (the whole grid frames between
  two positions) and `one_frame` (the grid's own first frame, which
  `Project::frame` is at every rate, 1/30 s only at a degenerate rate; spec
  §11 #174) count on the canvas's own grid at a rate the
  timescale does not divide (spec §11 #42).
- `time_bounds.rs` — the single structural-time admission checker and
  `MAX_STORED_TICKS`: ±9,000,000,000,000,000 for stored media, markers,
  clips, source positions and actions, including clip/action endpoints in
  i128. `Project::validate` and `format::write` both call it; vocabulary
  property timings and finite positive speeds are outside this envelope.
- `outcome.rs` — `Outcome`, the THREE arms every edit answers with
  (spec §5.5): applied with the new project, an identity, or refused with
  the rule's own sentence. An enum and its doc, nothing else. It is an enum
  rather than a side channel so that a site which has not decided which
  answer it gives does not compile; the fourth possibility, a request that
  could not be read, stays the `Err(String)` beside it. Its `Identity` doc
  is also the one place that says which non-edits speak and which stay
  identities on purpose (spec §5.5, §11 #88).
- `edit.rs` — the op enum, `parse` and `apply`. **Its module doc IS the op
  table's SEMANTICS half** — what each op means, and what an absent
  optional argument means — where `op_table.rs` is the ARGUMENTS half;
  `app/Sources/ReelOps.swift`'s typed builders, `AgentCatalog*.swift`'s
  tools and spec §6 mirror the two together. `OP_NAMES` is re-exported from
  here, at the path it has always had. `parse` answers an `Envelope` — the
  op AND the envelope's `scope` — and `apply_op(&Op)` knows nothing about
  nests. The semantics table is the reason this file is over the size cap
  and stays exempt (below).
- `op_table.rs` — the op table as DATA (road map 7's D3): one `OpRow` per
  op and one `Argument` per argument — its name, its `Kind` (`Kind::Output`
  for `set_canvas`'s dynamic range, `Kind::Blending` for its blending),
  whether the
  decoder requires it and, for the few that have one, its `Bound` — and
  `OP_NAMES` as a projection of it, re-exported by
  `edit.rs` so no caller moved. A published interface, where the `Op` enum
  and the dispatch are its implementation. Its one reader in the crate is
  `op_schema.rs`, which carries the rows out through the FFI; the APP's
  reader is every one of the sixty-four op tools in the agent catalog,
  which print these rows instead of restating them. **A `Bound` is
  published only where the core REFUSES outside it** — `set_canvas`'s two
  dimensions, sourced from `edit_canvas.rs`'s own constants, and
  `add_graphic_clip`'s `width` and `height`, from `model_graphic.rs`'s, never
  retyped — and never where it CLAMPS, which is the app's to say in its
  prose. A row holds no prose, no semantics and no default spelled twice;
  `Kind` is closed (twenty-three kinds; `Texts`, a list of strings, is
  `set_action_end`'s `off`), carries each vocabulary's members, and has exactly ONE
  kind per answer serde gives, because a distinction the
  decoder cannot see is one no test could prove. Nothing here is the
  authority — the enum's fields are, and `core/tests/op_table.rs` proves
  every row by asking the decoder. Capped at 400 lines like any new module:
  it does NOT inherit `edit.rs`'s table exemption.
- `op_schema.rs` — `op_table.rs` written as JSON Schema, which is what
  `rc_op_schemas` publishes (road map 7's D3·2): one object per op, its
  properties the arguments and its `required` the ones the decoder will not
  do without. **The match over `Kind` is exhaustive** — a kind added to the
  table does not compile until this says what JSON it is — and it is a
  module of its own because a row changes when an OP does and this changes
  when the published DIALECT does. It says nothing about what an argument is
  FOR (the catalog's prose), nothing about what a patch may CARRY
  (`Kind::Object` is an object with no properties; D1 left the core the one
  validator of that), and nothing about `additionalProperties` on an op,
  because the catalog merges `project` and `scope` in afterwards. Tested
  through the FFI in `core/tests/op_schemas.rs`.
- `scope.rs` — editing INSIDE a nest: the envelope's `scope` key. Builds a
  VIEW project from the nest (its tracks and clips at top level, its frozen
  size as the canvas, the parent's rate, media, `next_id` and nests, no
  markers), applies the op to it UNCHANGED, merges back. So `Project::clip`
  keeps its one meaning and no op has a nest-aware branch. Three things are
  counter-intuitive and measured: the scoped nest's own row stays in the view
  with its tracks and clips EMPTIED (removing it dangles every other nest's
  reference; leaving it whole doubles every id under `validate`); the nests
  write-back is union first, orphans after; and **a scoped apply has a wider
  `Err` arm than any unscoped op** — `check_caps` and `check_nesting` are
  document-wide and run on the MERGED parent, so an op valid inside the nest
  can still return `Err`. `refused_inside` is an EXHAUSTIVE match over every
  op, so a new op does not compile until it is classified. The READ half is
  `rc_project_scoped` in `ffi.rs`, which calls the same `scoped_view`.
- `edit_graphic.rs` — `add_graphic_clip` and `set_graphic`: every argument
  checked through `model_graphic.rs` BEFORE `edit_clip.rs`'s
  `add_described_clip` (`pub(crate)`, with `Described`) places the clip, so
  the op table's bound probe reaches the side check on any project;
  `set_graphic`'s patch reader takes `name`, `width`, `height`, `length`,
  `props` and refuses `in` by name. With a `schema`, a `null` for a prop
  an action on the clip names stores the schema's default (G-34 (d)).
- `edit_clip.rs` — clip construction and placement callers: `add_clip`, move,

  exactly the clip's speed (spec §11, #22 and D4-2 to D4-5); the other
  writers are `edit_canvas.rs`'s `resnap`, `edit_paste.rs`'s two loops,
  `edit_nest.rs`'s `unnest` and `edit_background.rs`'s timed plate. Over

- `edit_clip_timing.rs` — `trim_start`, `trim_end`, `rate_stretch`, `set_speed`,

  `set_speed` takes a `rate` or a `duration` (Fit to duration), exactly one.
  On a ramped clip (SR-19 (a), (b)) both rate edits scale the WHOLE profile

- `edit_detach.rs` — `detach_audio` and `set_enabled`, a clip's video and

- `edit_fit.rs` — `fit_scale` and `fill_scale` (Fit is a RESCUE for oversized

  (mutual, one container); `with_links` (the named clips, then each one's
  partner on an UNLOCKED track — `move_clips`, `split_clips`,

- `edit_commit.rs` — the placement commit protocol: replacements preserve
  caller order and check old tracks before destination tracks; additions
  check caller-allocated candidates against the input project; both write
  one draft and call `finish_placement`, which mints gained transitions on
  exactly the chosen tracks before `finish`. `finish` remains equality first,
  validation second, and does not itself refuse. `Clip::placed` is the one
  literal of a newly placed clip (each placing site overrides it by struct

- `edit_split.rs` — `split_clip` and what the SECOND clip inherits: base
  props from the evaluation at the cut, unfinished actions rebased, a
  straddled one narrowed, presets and motion halves anchored to the two
  ends. Every splitter in the crate routes here, so a rule stated once is a
  rule they all obey. A free function over `&mut Project` because it is
  called mid-edit on a clone the caller is still assembling.
  A graphic's second half gets `in + cut` through `recipe_graphic.rs`'s

- `edit_props.rs` — the five patches (`set_video`, `set_audio`, `set_text`,

  makes a video group storable — empty motion → null, `check_video`,
  identity curves dropped, `check_blend` / `check_adjustment_video` /
  `check_qualifier_clip` / `check_look_media`, `snap_motion` — run by

  `normalise_and_check_group` beside it (`settle_video` for a video group,

  patch or checked copied group carries on the frame grid AFTER the range

  `patch.rs`'s and nothing here restates it.
- `patch.rs` — reading a caller-authored patch, cut out of `edit_props.rs`

  walk of keys and JSON kinds, array indices in the path) and `merge_group`

  "absent keeps": a `video.filters` entry must name both its keys, because a

  here is handed a clip or a project: what a patch may carry is a fact about
  the vocabulary, which is `props_check.rs`'s reason for existing one step
  further on. `GROUPS` — every group in its order on `Clip`, the order

  `isolation` and format 32's `eq` (every slot, `bypass` true), `hum` and

  than the one a snap rounded it to. Gradient stops are deliberately NOT
  order-checked: a refusal would break dragging one stop past another

## Rules

**Modules and size.** New feature area = new module with its own
`impl Project` block. Soft cap ~600 lines; needing a new `// ---- name --`
banner section is the signal to split. Every module keeps a `//!` doc;
numeric and algorithmic choices get prose "why" comments. **A file at the cap
gives something up BEFORE it takes anything on**: the cut is a PURE MOVE,
landed and gated alone, so the feature's diff is attributable; budget the cut
against the pessimistic number, because an estimate here has run about two
thirds of the truth. Over the cap today and known debt, not licence:
`edit_clip.rs` and `edit.rs`, whose
standing exemption is that its module doc IS the op table's semantics half
(the cut there, if ever forced, is the `Op` enum into an `edit_ops.rs`, and
never in the same phase as a feature). The current list is `wc -l`; named
seams are in `designs/adr/core-file-history.md` "Named next cuts".

**Dependencies.** `serde` and `serde_json` (the JSON the FFI speaks),
`tiny_http` (the agent's socket), and `serde_path_to_error`, which is there
so a patch refusal names the path to what only the type can refuse (a
misspelt variant, a `null` a required field cannot take), where serde alone
names only the value. `graphic` (the path crate `../graphic`, road map
10's motion-graphics engine), named by `ffi_graphic.rs` alone. It enables
`serde_json`'s `preserve_order`, and a feature is unified across a path
dependency, so the core's `serde_json` has it too; `Cargo.toml` spells it
out. `svgtypes` 0.16.1 (usvg's own pin, already in the lock) for its
named-colour table only, so a stored name agrees with what usvg draws
(`model_color.rs`). `sha2` for the `.fjgraphic` manifest's checksums
(G-46; also `graphic_ffi.rs`'s revision oracle).

**One implementation per algorithm.** Before writing time math, find the
existing implementation and route through it. Shared constants have exactly
one home (`TIMESCALE` in `time.rs`; `RC_*` caps in `format.rs`; the
inspector's bounds in `props_check.rs`).

**Purity.** Every edit takes `&self` and returns a new value — internally
clone-then-mutate. An op that would change nothing returns
`Outcome::Identity`, never an identical copy: an identical copy registers a
phantom undo step in the app.

**Errors.** Every edit answers `Result<Outcome, String>` — three arms and
one tier, no error enum. `Outcome::Applied` = the new project;
`Outcome::Identity` = the op is valid and nothing needed to change;
`Outcome::Refused(String)` = a rule declined it, carrying the rule's OWN
sentence rather than a second one written at the call site; `Err(String)` =
invalid arguments, unknown ids, parse failures — lowercase messages naming
the offending value. A refusal is not an error tier: both middle arms leave
the project untouched and register no undo step. No input may panic. FFI
mapping (`ffi_edit.rs`): `Applied` → a new handle; `Identity` → NULL with
neither channel written; `Refused` → NULL with the sentence through
`reason_out`; `Err` → NULL with the message through `err_out`; caught panic
→ `"internal error: <what>"`. The two channels are never both written.

**Times.** Every tick value that reaches the model is snapped to the
document's frame grid before it is stored (`time::snap_to_frame`). Never
store a sub-frame time. Where a range check names the value, the check runs
on what the CALLER sent and the snap follows it, so a refusal never names a
number the door rounded to (`props_check.rs`, `edit_props.rs`'s
`snap_motion` / `snap_animation`). The one family that is deliberately NOT
on the grid is the audio ramps — `audio.fade_in` / `fade_out`, the duck's
and the compressor's attack and release — because they are envelope lengths
sampled at the audio rate, not positions in the picture, and quantising them
to a video frame would round a 10 ms attack to nothing. The other is a SHIFT
(spec §11 #42): an op that moves several clips — the ripples, `close_gap`,
`insert_time`, `move_clip` — moves them all by ONE delta so abutments stay
exact, and at a rate whose frame is not a whole number of ticks (7 fps) a
moved start may sit a tick off the grid; a canvas rate change re-snaps (D7-3).

**FFI exports.** Every export: `#[no_mangle] pub unsafe extern "C"`, a `///`
comment restating the header contract, a `/// # Safety` paragraph, NULL
tolerance first, narrow `unsafe {}` blocks. Route through the shared helpers
in `ffi_util.rs` — a freshly hand-rolled `catch_unwind` is a review flag.
Export names mirror the Rust method exactly.

**Format changes.** Any change to persisted project state bumps
`RC_FORMAT_VERSION` in `format.rs` **and** the `#define` in
`core/include/framejob_core.h`; the reader must keep accepting every prior
version; the writer enforces the reader's caps. A bump whose new fields all
carry a serde default needs no migrate step (versions 3 through 15 have none;
15's one step only renumbers the branch's 1015)
but still bumps, because unknown keys are ignored at every level by design
and an older build would otherwise open the file, drop the new fields on read
and write the loss back on the next save; a bump that changes a field's
SHAPE adds a step at the migration hook (`migrate_1_to_2`). Each bump gets a
`schema_vN.rs` test that opens the previous versions' fixtures and reads the
new keys' ORDER off the written text, since a parsed `Value` sorts them.
**Nothing that checks the version writes the current number as a
literal**, so a bump edits `format.rs` (and `format_history.rs`'s paragraph)
and the header and no test or proof:
- The "one past the current version, refused" tests in
  `core/tests/schema_v3.rs` and `core/tests/model_tests.rs` compute
  `RC_FORMAT_VERSION + 1` and assert the refusal's whole message with
  both numbers.
- `schema_v3.rs`'s `the_header_states_the_same_format_version_as_the_core`
  holds the header's `#define` to `format.rs`'s constant, so a bump that
  moves only one of them fails `make test`.
- The schema tests' and `model_tests.rs`'s `/version` assertions read
  `RC_FORMAT_VERSION`; `schema_v10.rs`'s byte-for-byte round trips rewrite
  the fixture's version line through its `current()` helper.
- The proof scripts (`tools/proof/*_proof.py`) read the HEADER's number
  through a `format_version()` helper. `phase9`'s "one past" fixture is
  `format_version() + 1`, and its every-version loop runs up to the current
  version. A proof that expected a literal would fail weeks later, in
  someone else's session, with nothing pointing at the bump.

A fixture's own version (`e2_proof.py`'s `VERSION = 8`, a
`schema_vN.rs`'s older files) is a literal on purpose. One claim still
moves with the schema rather than the number: when a bump appends a key to
the video object, `schema_v4.rs`'s text assertion about what follows
`obscure` fails in `make test` and names the new neighbour.

**Tests.** All tests are black-box in `core/tests/` (no `#[cfg(test)]` in
`src/`), exercised **through the FFI** wherever possible, and verified
against independently written oracles — never golden files. Shared helpers
live in `tests/common/` (`content` / `contents` — "the same clips, ids
aside" — is the one spelling of that comparison, used by `nest`'s identity
claim and `scope`'s oracle alike); new feature area = new test file. Every
new export gets at least one test plus inclusion in the null-safety sweep.
Finish Rust work with `cargo fmt` and a clean `make lint`.

### Decisions to record or amend

Each decision is recorded in `designs/spec/11-decisions/creator-jobs.md` before its phase's
code. Draft text follows.

#### Amended (draft amending text, appended to each entry)

1. **recording.md, first bullet ("… the cursor, and a ring around each click — is taken;
   nothing is reconstructed afterwards").** CJ-1 already lifts its "callouts stay OUT"; this
   amends what CJ-1 leaves standing. Append:

   > **Amended by CU-1** (creator-jobs CU0a): the cursor's path and images, every click and
   > scroll, and — opt-in, under Input Monitoring — the shortcuts pressed and the times of other
   > key presses are recorded as DATA in a cursor file beside each movie. With Cursor set to
   > Separate (the default from CU3c) ScreenCaptureKit draws neither the pointer nor the click
   > ring, and the editor draws the cursor as part of the screen clip's layer. Nothing is
   > reconstructed for a recording that has no cursor file.

2. **recording.md, second bullet ("A recording is ordinary media … The model learns nothing:
   no source kind, no flag, no schema bump").** Append:

   > **Amended by CU-2** (creator-jobs CU0a): a screen recording's movie may carry a cursor file,
   > which import attaches as `media.cursor` (one format bump, CU3a, written only when set). It
   > is still imported through `adoptImported` and the two-try placement, there is still no
   > source kind and no flag on a clip, and every op, cache and export but the frame recipe
   > treats it as the media clip it is. A media without one draws exactly as before.

3. **recording.md, "The panel asks for the grants; the tool never does".** Append:

   > **Extended by CU-3**: Input Monitoring (`kTCCServiceListenEvent`) is the recorder's fourth
   > grant, after Screen Recording, Microphone and Camera. It is read and asked only when the
   > person chose to record shortcuts (CJ-4).

4. **recording.md, the voice-over bullet.** Two changes:
   - *Refused arguments.* `record_screen`'s screen-only arguments gain `cursor` (CU3c), `keys`
     (CU6) and the three landing arguments (CU10). With `source: "voice_over"` they are
     refused by name, in that order, after `include_framejob_windows`. The same list is added
     to CAM-4 (3)'s list for `source: "camera"`.
   - *The status item.* "No microphone glyph in the menu bar" stands. **Amended by CU-61**:
     while shortcuts are recorded, the status item carries a keyboard mark after the dot.

5. **CAM-9 (3) ("The watch is on the stream only with a camera").** Append:

   > **Amended by CU-13**: the watch is on the stream with a camera or with cursor data (every
   > display, window or picked recording from CU1b), and besides E2 it records each complete
   > frame's geometry when it changes; CAM-9 (6)'s remove-and-re-add around a resume applies
   > whenever it is on.

6. **The recorder's "Show Clicks needs BGRA" (R0 q6a).** This is a code-doc rule in
   `RecordingSetup.swift:34–38`, not an entry. CU-31 restates it: BGRA and `showMouseClicks`
   only with Cursor In the picture. With Cursor Separate, Show Clicks means "land the clips
   with click ripples on".

CJ-1 lifts CAM-1's "callouts stay OUT"; nothing here repeats it.

**Not amended, and nothing here re-litigates them.**
- G-1 (nothing else scriptable). R5-1 (closed vocabularies). AU-2 (third-party Audio Units out).
- AI-10 (an agent turn is its undo steps).
- CAM-10 (the camera's corner; bet 6's).
- **D4-6** (the reversed mirror is app arithmetic with one home). The cursor's mirror is
  `ReverseMirror.swift`'s fourth reader (CU-32); the core keeps none.
- **AU-94** (rate ops refused on a linked pair). `retime_range` refuses a linked clip in its
  range in AU-94's own sentence (CU-90).
- **CI-3** (base-only rows routed by the inspector; the core's door unchanged). The recipe reads
  `smoothing` and `hide_idle` from the clip's base props, as `audio_track.rs` reads a base
  `audio.mono` (CU-30); `set_action_end` still takes them.
- **CO-61, CO-62**. Auto Zoom's refusal of a placed clip (CU-75) is the other direction of
  CO-62, and both point at a nest.
- **The root `CLAUDE.md`'s FFI rule**: `ReelCore.swift` stays the only file that calls `rc_*`
  (CU-9).
- The rest of recording.md and camera-recording*.md.

#### New in CU0a (CU-1…CU-9)

- **CU-1 — Scope: the cursor, clicks and scrolls are data; shortcuts are opt-in; the editor
  draws the cursor** (owner, 2026-11-01). It amends recording.md's first bullet as above. CJ-1
  covers callouts.
  - Zooms, overlays and speed-ups are generated as ordinary edits.
  - **Old recordings behave as today.** No cursor is reconstructed for a recording without a
    cursor file, or for any imported screen video. No vision pass looks for a pointer.
- **CU-2 — The cursor file.** One file per segment movie, named `<movie stem>.fjcursor`, beside
  the movie in `~/Movies/Frame Job Recordings/`. It amends recording.md's second bullet.
  - **The core owns the format.** Its module doc (`cursor_file.rs`) is the specification.
    Swift writes the file, and the core reads it back before it is renamed into place. That
    read-back is how the two sides are held to one format.
  - **It is versioned.** The core reads every version up to its own and refuses a newer one
    by name.
  - **Two sizes.** The header carries the stream's content size (its configured points × pixels
    per point) and `movie_size`, the written movie's track size, read back from the movie at
    the segment's close. The encoder rounds an odd dimension up to even, so the two can
    differ; the mapping uses the first and import matches the second.
  - It is attached at import as `media.cursor = {path, bookmark?, in_picture}`.
- **CU-3 — Input Monitoring, the recorder's fourth grant.**
  - Read by `CGPreflightListenEventAccess()`.
  - Asked by `CGRequestListenEventAccess()` from the panel only, and only when the person
    chose to record shortcuts and pressed Record.
  - **Asked once.** `FrameJobInputMonitoringAsked` is remembered under the Screen Recording
    rule's terms: counted only in a launchd-owned launch, and `launchClause` appended to every
    sentence. After that, each press opens `Privacy_ListenEvent`.
  - `record_screen` reads the grant and refuses `keys` with the sentence "Input Monitoring is
    not granted to Frame Job. Turn it on in System Settings ▸ Privacy & Security ▸ Input
    Monitoring." plus "then relaunch Frame Job." only when CU-S1's verdict is
    `relaunch=needed`, plus `launchClause`.
  - **Accessibility is never asked for**, and Frame Job never posts an event.
  - **No Info.plist key or entitlement**, unless spike CU-S1 measures one is needed.
- **CU-4 — The cursor is part of its clip's layer, not a clip of its own.**
  - The layer stage composites the cursor sprite and its ripples over the source texel inside
    `layerSample` (`Compositor.metal:800`), the one function every tap of the stage reads its
    source through, and before `gradeSample`. So crop, placement, grade, filters, the
    spotlight, obscure regions, mattes and transitions meet the cursor as they met a burned
    one. It follows every transform, zoom action, nest and speed ramp the clip has.
  - The sprite is bound at `texture(5)`, the slot CJ-8 (b) reserves. No copy of the frame is
    made, and no pipeline is added.
  - A sprite on another track would drift on the first trim, slip or speed change, which is
    why it is not one.
  - The core computes the cursor's source time and its state. The compositor draws, and never
    opens a file or computes a path: a track it needs and does not have yet is not drawn
    (CU-37).
- **CU-5 — Planners live in the core, and their results are ordinary ops.** Auto zoom,
  shortcut overlays and typing stretches are pure functions of the cursor file and the
  project. Each answers a list of existing ops (and CU9a's one new op), which Swift applies as
  one named undo step.
  - **No action or clip is tagged "generated."** There is no format change for it.
  - **Re-planning finds zooms by content.** It recognises a zoom action by the core's twin of
    `ActionBands.isZoom` (CU7). A probe row holds the two tests to one answer.
  - **A reversed clip is refused by name** by every planner and by `get_cursor_events` in clip
    time ("clip C plays reversed; <command> plans only clips that play forward"), because
    mapping its times would put a mirror in the core (D4-6).
- **CU-6 — The spikes' rules are fixed before their runs.** These are the rules under
  "Spikes", below (CJ-7).
  - Each instrument stores this file's SHA-256 as `rule_sha256` in its `results.json`, as
    CAM-2 did.
  - A spike's verdict is recorded here before the phase that depends on it starts.
- **CU-7 — Keys are private by construction.**
  - **What is recorded.** A key-down while ⌘ or ⌃ is held is a shortcut, stored with its
    spelled keys. Every other key-down, and every auto-repeat, is a mark with a time and no
    identity. No character, key code or label of a typed key is ever stored, so none can reach
    a tool answer, the project, or the Assistant's model.
  - **Secure input.** Nothing is recorded, not even timing, while any process holds secure
    input (`IsSecureEventInputEnabled()`). A password field that does not turn secure input on
    — a Terminal `sudo` prompt without Secure Keyboard Entry, or a web or custom field in some
    apps (Apple TN2150: secure input is a process's own opt-in) — is recorded like any other
    typing: as time-only marks.
  - **No "all keys" mode.** Its one use, typed text as overlays, would put whatever was typed
    into the project, where every tool and the Assistant read it, including a password typed
    where secure input was off. It is not built in this bet.
  - **It is visible.** The status item carries a keyboard mark while shortcuts are recorded
    (CU-61).
- **CU-8 — No recorder's code is carried over.**
  - Cap is AGPL-3.0, and the Concat rule applies to it.
  - OpenScreen (MIT) and every other recorder are not carried either.
  - Algorithms here are written from their stated rules.
- **CU-9 — The FFI surface is three exports, and their wrapper pays for its room.**
  - The core exports `rc_cursor_open(bytes, len, err_out)` (parse and validate, answering an
    `RcCursor *`; a check is an open and a free), `rc_cursor_free`, and
    `rc_cursor_query(tracks, n, project, request_json, err_out)`. Every read — a frame's
    state, an image, events, the path, and each planner — is one JSON request and one JSON
    answer through the query. `project` may be NULL for the requests that need no project. A
    plan over several clips passes several tracks. An image is answered as base64 PNG inside
    the JSON.
  - The Swift side is `ReelCursor` in `ReelCore.swift`: its init, its `deinit` and one `query`
    method, about 30 lines. Every typed decoding of an answer lives in `CursorValues.swift`,
    which names no `rc_*` symbol (the `CoreValues.swift` shape).
  - **The rule is not amended.** `ReelCore.swift` stays the only file that calls `rc_*`.
    CU1a pays for the room first with a doc-only cut gated alone, as codec-export C3, G-46 and
    G-47 did, and the file ends CU2 no longer than its 766 lines.
  - CJ's table row for `ReelCore.swift` reads "any new `rc_*` (none planned here)". The
    integrator corrects it to "CU's three `rc_cursor_*` exports (CU-9); paid by CU1a".
  - **Why not a `ReelCore+Cursor.swift` that may call `rc_*`:** it would change a rule carried
    from Rasterize for one bet, while three exports fit the rule as it stands.
  - The bumps (CU3a, CU11) are provisional under CJ-6.

Later phases record their own blocks (CU-10… onward) before their code. A phase split by size

### Spikes

Every spike is a probe or an instrument under `tools/proof/cursor_spike/`, run in CU0b.
Probes compile through `tools/proof/swift_build.py`. Any row whose grant is held by a
launched `.app` runs in a scratch hardened-runtime bundle opened with `open -a`, because a
shell launch is attributed to the terminal (R0 q1). Posting input needs Accessibility for the
poster. Rows that post input are skipped by name when the terminal lacks it, and a person's
run covers them once.

- **CU-S1 — Capture APIs, grants, clocks, the cursor's image.** Runs before CU1a.
  - *Question:*
    - Which API delivers mouse clicks, scrolls and (polled) positions with no grant?
    - Which delivers key-down, key-up and flags-changed with Input Monitoring alone?
    - What clock do event timestamps use?
    - Does `NSCursor.currentSystem` report another application's cursor, and at what cost?
    - What does a hidden cursor report?
    - What does secure input withhold?
  - *Rows:*
    - **A1:** a listen-only `CGEventTap` (session tap) for mouse down/up (left, right,
      other), dragged and scroll, with no grant.
    - **A2:** the same tap for key events: no grant, Input Monitoring only, Accessibility only.
    - **A3:** `NSEvent` global and local monitors, the same matrix.
    - **A4:** `CGEvent(source: nil)?.location` polled at 120 Hz: µs per call, and whether
      `CGWarpMouseCursorPosition` moves are seen.
    - **A5:** `NSCursor.currentSystem` over TextEdit's text, a Safari link and a resize edge:
      image identity, hot spot, reps, ms per call (image plus TIFF hash), the thread it is
      safe on, and whether it ever answers nil.
    - **A6:** event timestamp against arrival `mach_absolute_time`, as nanoseconds, as mach
      units, and as `systemUptime`.
    - **A7:** keys delivered while the probe holds `EnableSecureEventInput()`.
    - **A8:** whether the signed bundle needs any plist key or entitlement for ListenEvent, and
      whether a tap created before the grant works without a relaunch after it.
    - **A9:** a hidden cursor: a helper process calls `NSCursor.hide()`, and TextEdit hides the
      pointer while typing (`setHiddenUntilMouseMoves`). What `currentSystem`, its image and
      `CGCursorIsVisible()` report in each case, 10 trials each.
    - **A10:** a replacement for `currentSystem`: two 64 × 64 pt `SCStream`s on a region
      around the pointer, one with `showsCursor` on and one off, differenced; the silhouette
      against `currentSystem`'s image as intersection over union, 10 trials each over A5's
      three cursors.
  - *Rule:*
    - **Positions** are polled (A4) if a poll costs ≤ 20 µs median and sees warps and real
      moves. Otherwise they come from the event source chosen for clicks.
    - **Clicks and scrolls** use the tap if it delivers ≥ 99 % of 200 events with no grant,
      Frame Job's own windows included. Otherwise they use global+local monitors if those do.
      If neither does, **STOP**: clicks are not captured, and the owner is asked before CU1a.
    - **Keys** use the tap if it delivers under Input Monitoring alone, else the monitors if
      they do. If keys need Accessibility, **STOP key capture** (CU6 is not built) and the
      owner is asked.
    - **The image sampler** asks at most 10 times a second plus once at each mouse-down.
      **`cursor_image=current-system`** if A5 identifies another app's I-beam and pointing
      hand in ≥ 9 of 10 trials and its median cost × 10 Hz is ≤ 1 % of one core (≤ 1 ms a
      call). Otherwise `none`: the file records no images, and the cursor draws as Frame Job's
      arrow.
    - **A nil at run time.** Whatever the verdict, the recorder checks every sample for nil. A
      nil sample records no image change. A segment whose every sample was nil writes
      `cursor_image: none`, draws the arrow, and the landing note says so.
    - **Hidden cursors.** If a signal from A9 tells hidden from shown in ≥ 9 of 10 trials in
      both cases, the file records `hidden` spans and the editor draws no cursor in them
      (`hidden=recorded`). Otherwise hidden spans are not recorded, Hide when idle is the
      remedy, and the verdict records the limit for the owner (`hidden=not-recorded`).
    - **The replacement.** A10 is measured, not built. If A5 fails and A10's IoU is ≥ 0.9 in
      ≥ 9 of 10 trials, CU1b builds A10's capture as the image source (`image_fallback=a10`).
      Otherwise the arrow stands (`image_fallback=arrow`), and an issue is filed with A10's
      numbers for the day `currentSystem` answers nil.
    - **The event clock** is the hypothesis whose arrival minus event time lies in [0, 20 ms]
      for ≥ 99 % of events.
    - **Secure input:** delivered keys are noted, and the recorder drops them by
      `IsSecureEventInputEnabled()` either way (CU-7).
  - *Verdict line:*
    `VERDICT positions=<poll|events> clicks=<tap|monitor|STOP> keys=<tap|monitor|STOP> cursor_image=<current-system|none> hidden=<recorded|not-recorded> image_fallback=<a10|arrow> event_clock=<ns|mach|uptime> secure=<withheld|delivered> relaunch=<needed|not-needed>`.
- **CU-S2 — From global points to movie pixels, and the time anchor.** Runs before CU1a.
  - *Question:* which mapping from a polled global position (Quartz points, top-left origin)
    to the movie's pixels is right for each source, and which anchor puts the samples on the
    movie's clock, with the pointer in the picture and with Separate's configuration?
  - *Instrument, In the picture:*
    - It records with `showsCursor = true` over a flat-colour full-screen window of its own.
      The burned cursor's tip is the truth, found per decoded frame by thresholding against
      the flat colour.
    - It warps the cursor along a known path.
    - It logs every frame's `SCStreamFrameInfo` and the polled samples.
  - *Instrument, Separate:* Separate's exact configuration (`showsCursor = false`,
    `showMouseClicks = false`, 420v). The pointer no longer dirties the screen, so the truth
    is a marker of the instrument's own: a 24 pt square in a contrasting colour whose top-left
    corner the instrument moves to the warped point at each step, found per decoded frame. The
    screen therefore changes at every step, as a moving window would.
  - *Still start, Separate:* the instrument holds the screen still for 2 s while the cursor
    moves, then flips a full-screen flat field's colour at a host time it logs. The first
    frame showing the flip gives the movie time of that host time. It records which anchor the
    segment used (E2 or E1) and the anchor's error.
  - *Sources:* a display at Nominal; a display at Best (2×); the instrument's own window, moved
    and then resized during the recording; a window of odd size (1001 × 701 pt at 1×); a
    picked window; a second display when attached (skipped by name otherwise). Each source
    runs in both configurations.
  - *Candidates:*
    - **M1.** `pixel = (p − screenRect.origin) × contentScale × pixelsPerPoint +
      contentRect.origin × pixelsPerPoint`, with pixelsPerPoint = the stream's configured
      pixel width ÷ its point width. An encoder's padding column lies outside the content.
    - **M2.** M1 with `scaleFactor` in place of pixelsPerPoint.
    - **M3.** A fixed display frame from `SCDisplay.frame` (for display sources).
    - Anchors: E2, E1 and `DisplayTime` of the first complete frame.
  - *Rule:*
    - **Mapping.** The first of M1, M2, M3 whose tip error is ≤ 1.5 movie px at the 95th
      percentile on every source row, odd window included, over still frames, wins.
    - **Anchor.** The first of E2, E1 and DisplayTime whose time error is ≤ one frame interval
      at the 95th percentile on every row of BOTH configurations, measured over moving frames
      by the position error divided by the speed there.
    - **Still start.** E1's error over 10 still-start runs is ≤ 25 ms at the 95th percentile
      (#370's 21 ms and a margin). If it is not, the limit is recorded and the file still
      names E1.
    - **STOP.** If no candidate passes for window sources, window recordings keep the cursor
      burned in. The panel greys Separate for Window, and the owner is told. If none passes
      for displays, the bet stops after CU1b. If a candidate passes In the picture and fails
      only Separate, Separate is not the default (CU-36 makes In the picture the default) and
      the owner is told.
- **CU-S3 — Do dirty rects locate typing?** Runs before CU1a, because CU1a's file either
  stores dirty-rect boxes or does not.
  - *Instrument:*
    - It records its own `NSTextView` while text is inserted programmatically, so no key event
      is needed.
    - Distractors run at the same time: the menu-bar clock, a spinner elsewhere, and a playing
      animation in another window.
    - Per burst it takes the median centre of the per-frame dirty-rect bounding boxes, against
      the caret rect the text view reports.
  - *Rule:*
    - **Pass** if within 64 pt of the caret in ≥ 9 of 10 bursts. CU1a's file then stores each
      complete frame's dirty-rect bounding box, and CU7 aims typing zooms at their median
      centre.
    - **Fail** otherwise: nothing about dirty rects is stored, and typing zooms aim at the
      last click before the burst, else the cursor's position at its start.
- **CU-S4 — The file's size and speed.** Runs on synthetic files.
  - *Instrument:* the core's reader prototype over a worst case: one hour of continuous
    movement sampled at 120 Hz (432,000 samples), 3,600 clicks, 20,000 key marks, 40 images.
    Each figure is measured through a JSON request and answer, as `rc_cursor_query` will run
    it.
  - *Rule:*
    - **JSON** (columnar integer microseconds and points ×100) if all three hold:
      - the file is ≤ 25 MB;
      - parse and validate take ≤ 300 ms;
      - `state at t` takes ≤ 20 µs median, request and answer included, once prepared.
    - **Otherwise a binary columnar body** (little-endian i64 arrays after a JSON header),
      version 1 either way.
    - **Smoothing's precompute** (`prepare` at smoothing 1) takes ≤ 1 s on the one-hour file.
      If it does not, smoothing is prepared per 60 s window on demand, still off the
      compositor's thread (CU-37), and the verdict says which.
- **CU-S5 — Motion blur's cost.** Runs before CU11; it may run any time after CU0b.
  - *Instrument:* a probe through `MetalRenderer`'s pipelines draws one full-canvas layer N
    times at sub-frame transforms (a 2× zoom's middle, eased), accumulated in `rgba16Float`,
    for N ∈ {4, 8, 16}, at 1920×1080 and 3840×2160. It measures GPU time per frame against
    the same frame drawn once.
  - *Rule:*
    - **Ship zoom blur** at the largest N in {16, 8, 4} whose added GPU time is ≤ 4 ms at 1080p
      and ≤ 8 ms at 4K on the owner's Mac, in preview and export alike (parity: one N).
    - **STOP zoom blur** if N = 4 misses either bound. The numbers are recorded and an issue is
      filed. Cursor blur, N sprite samples inside `layerSample`, ships either way.

#### New in CU0a (CU-1…CU-9)

- **CU-1 — Scope: the cursor, clicks and scrolls are data; shortcuts are opt-in; the editor
  draws the cursor** (owner, 2026-11-01). It amends recording.md's first bullet as above. CJ-1
  covers callouts.
  - Zooms, overlays and speed-ups are generated as ordinary edits.
  - **Old recordings behave as today.** No cursor is reconstructed for a recording without a
    cursor file, or for any imported screen video. No vision pass looks for a pointer.
- **CU-2 — The cursor file.** One file per segment movie, named `<movie stem>.fjcursor`, beside
  the movie in `~/Movies/Frame Job Recordings/`. It amends recording.md's second bullet.
  - **The core owns the format.** Its module doc (`cursor_file.rs`) is the specification.
    Swift writes the file, and the core reads it back before it is renamed into place. That
    read-back is how the two sides are held to one format.
  - **It is versioned.** The core reads every version up to its own and refuses a newer one
    by name.
  - **Two sizes.** The header carries the stream's content size (its configured points × pixels
    per point) and `movie_size`, the written movie's track size, read back from the movie at
    the segment's close. The encoder rounds an odd dimension up to even, so the two can
    differ; the mapping uses the first and import matches the second.
  - It is attached at import as `media.cursor = {path, bookmark?, in_picture}`.
- **CU-3 — Input Monitoring, the recorder's fourth grant.**
  - Read by `CGPreflightListenEventAccess()`.
  - Asked by `CGRequestListenEventAccess()` from the panel only, and only when the person
    chose to record shortcuts and pressed Record.
  - **Asked once.** `FrameJobInputMonitoringAsked` is remembered under the Screen Recording
    rule's terms: counted only in a launchd-owned launch, and `launchClause` appended to every
    sentence. After that, each press opens `Privacy_ListenEvent`.
  - `record_screen` reads the grant and refuses `keys` with the sentence "Input Monitoring is
    not granted to Frame Job. Turn it on in System Settings ▸ Privacy & Security ▸ Input
    Monitoring." plus "then relaunch Frame Job." only when CU-S1's verdict is
    `relaunch=needed`, plus `launchClause`.
  - **Accessibility is never asked for**, and Frame Job never posts an event.
  - **No Info.plist key or entitlement**, unless spike CU-S1 measures one is needed.
- **CU-4 — The cursor is part of its clip's layer, not a clip of its own.**
  - The layer stage composites the cursor sprite and its ripples over the source texel inside
    `layerSample` (`Compositor.metal:800`), the one function every tap of the stage reads its
    source through, and before `gradeSample`. So crop, placement, grade, filters, the
    spotlight, obscure regions, mattes and transitions meet the cursor as they met a burned
    one. It follows every transform, zoom action, nest and speed ramp the clip has.
  - The sprite is bound at `texture(5)`, the slot CJ-8 (b) reserves. No copy of the frame is
    made, and no pipeline is added.
  - A sprite on another track would drift on the first trim, slip or speed change, which is
    why it is not one.
  - The core computes the cursor's source time and its state. The compositor draws, and never
    opens a file or computes a path: a track it needs and does not have yet is not drawn
    (CU-37).
- **CU-5 — Planners live in the core, and their results are ordinary ops.** Auto zoom,
  shortcut overlays and typing stretches are pure functions of the cursor file and the
  project. Each answers a list of existing ops (and CU9a's one new op), which Swift applies as
  one named undo step.
  - **No action or clip is tagged "generated."** There is no format change for it.
  - **Re-planning finds zooms by content.** It recognises a zoom action by the core's twin of
    `ActionBands.isZoom` (CU7). A probe row holds the two tests to one answer.
  - **A reversed clip is refused by name** by every planner and by `get_cursor_events` in clip
    time ("clip C plays reversed; <command> plans only clips that play forward"), because
    mapping its times would put a mirror in the core (D4-6).
- **CU-6 — The spikes' rules are fixed before their runs.** These are the rules under
  "Spikes", below (CJ-7).
  - Each instrument stores this file's SHA-256 as `rule_sha256` in its `results.json`, as
    CAM-2 did.
  - A spike's verdict is recorded here before the phase that depends on it starts.
- **CU-7 — Keys are private by construction.**
  - **What is recorded.** A key-down while ⌘ or ⌃ is held is a shortcut, stored with its
    spelled keys. Every other key-down, and every auto-repeat, is a mark with a time and no
    identity. No character, key code or label of a typed key is ever stored, so none can reach
    a tool answer, the project, or the Assistant's model.
  - **Secure input.** Nothing is recorded, not even timing, while any process holds secure
    input (`IsSecureEventInputEnabled()`). A password field that does not turn secure input on
    — a Terminal `sudo` prompt without Secure Keyboard Entry, or a web or custom field in some
    apps (Apple TN2150: secure input is a process's own opt-in) — is recorded like any other
    typing: as time-only marks.
  - **No "all keys" mode.** Its one use, typed text as overlays, would put whatever was typed
    into the project, where every tool and the Assistant read it, including a password typed
    where secure input was off. It is not built in this bet.
  - **It is visible.** The status item carries a keyboard mark while shortcuts are recorded
    (CU-61).
- **CU-8 — No recorder's code is carried over.**
  - Cap is AGPL-3.0, and the Concat rule applies to it.
  - OpenScreen (MIT) and every other recorder are not carried either.
  - Algorithms here are written from their stated rules.
- **CU-9 — The FFI surface is three exports, and their wrapper pays for its room.**
  - The core exports `rc_cursor_open(bytes, len, err_out)` (parse and validate, answering an
    `RcCursor *`; a check is an open and a free), `rc_cursor_free`, and
    `rc_cursor_query(tracks, n, project, request_json, err_out)`. Every read — a frame's
    state, an image, events, the path, and each planner — is one JSON request and one JSON
    answer through the query. `project` may be NULL for the requests that need no project. A
    plan over several clips passes several tracks. An image is answered as base64 PNG inside
    the JSON.

    method, about 30 lines. Every typed decoding of an answer lives in `CursorValues.swift`,
    which names no `rc_*` symbol (the `CoreValues.swift` shape).
  - **The rule is not amended.** `ReelCore.swift` stays the only file that calls `rc_*`.
    CU1a pays for the room first with a doc-only cut gated alone, as codec-export C3, G-46 and

### Spikes

Every spike is a probe or an instrument under `tools/proof/cursor_spike/`, run in CU0b.
Probes compile through `tools/proof/swift_build.py`. Any row whose grant is held by a
launched `.app` runs in a scratch hardened-runtime bundle opened with `open -a`, because a
shell launch is attributed to the terminal (R0 q1). Posting input needs Accessibility for the
poster. Rows that post input are skipped by name when the terminal lacks it, and a person's
run covers them once.

- **CU-S1 — Capture APIs, grants, clocks, the cursor's image.** Runs before CU1a.
  - *Question:*
    - Which API delivers mouse clicks, scrolls and (polled) positions with no grant?
    - Which delivers key-down, key-up and flags-changed with Input Monitoring alone?
    - What clock do event timestamps use?
    - Does `NSCursor.currentSystem` report another application's cursor, and at what cost?
    - What does a hidden cursor report?
    - What does secure input withhold?
  - *Rows:*
    - **A1:** a listen-only `CGEventTap` (session tap) for mouse down/up (left, right,
      other), dragged and scroll, with no grant.
    - **A2:** the same tap for key events: no grant, Input Monitoring only, Accessibility only.
    - **A3:** `NSEvent` global and local monitors, the same matrix.
    - **A4:** `CGEvent(source: nil)?.location` polled at 120 Hz: µs per call, and whether
      `CGWarpMouseCursorPosition` moves are seen.
    - **A5:** `NSCursor.currentSystem` over TextEdit's text, a Safari link and a resize edge:
      image identity, hot spot, reps, ms per call (image plus TIFF hash), the thread it is
      safe on, and whether it ever answers nil.
    - **A6:** event timestamp against arrival `mach_absolute_time`, as nanoseconds, as mach
      units, and as `systemUptime`.
    - **A7:** keys delivered while the probe holds `EnableSecureEventInput()`.
    - **A8:** whether the signed bundle needs any plist key or entitlement for ListenEvent, and
      whether a tap created before the grant works without a relaunch after it.
    - **A9:** a hidden cursor: a helper process calls `NSCursor.hide()`, and TextEdit hides the
      pointer while typing (`setHiddenUntilMouseMoves`). What `currentSystem`, its image and
      `CGCursorIsVisible()` report in each case, 10 trials each.
    - **A10:** a replacement for `currentSystem`: two 64 × 64 pt `SCStream`s on a region
      around the pointer, one with `showsCursor` on and one off, differenced; the silhouette
      against `currentSystem`'s image as intersection over union, 10 trials each over A5's
      three cursors.
  - *Rule:*
    - **Positions** are polled (A4) if a poll costs ≤ 20 µs median and sees warps and real
      moves. Otherwise they come from the event source chosen for clicks.
    - **Clicks and scrolls** use the tap if it delivers ≥ 99 % of 200 events with no grant,
      Frame Job's own windows included. Otherwise they use global+local monitors if those do.
      If neither does, **STOP**: clicks are not captured, and the owner is asked before CU1a.
    - **Keys** use the tap if it delivers under Input Monitoring alone, else the monitors if
      they do. If keys need Accessibility, **STOP key capture** (CU6 is not built) and the
      owner is asked.
    - **The image sampler** asks at most 10 times a second plus once at each mouse-down.
      **`cursor_image=current-system`** if A5 identifies another app's I-beam and pointing
      hand in ≥ 9 of 10 trials and its median cost × 10 Hz is ≤ 1 % of one core (≤ 1 ms a
      call). Otherwise `none`: the file records no images, and the cursor draws as Frame Job's
      arrow.
    - **A nil at run time.** Whatever the verdict, the recorder checks every sample for nil. A
      nil sample records no image change. A segment whose every sample was nil writes
      `cursor_image: none`, draws the arrow, and the landing note says so.
    - **Hidden cursors.** If a signal from A9 tells hidden from shown in ≥ 9 of 10 trials in
      both cases, the file records `hidden` spans and the editor draws no cursor in them
      (`hidden=recorded`). Otherwise hidden spans are not recorded, Hide when idle is the
      remedy, and the verdict records the limit for the owner (`hidden=not-recorded`).
    - **The replacement.** A10 is measured, not built. If A5 fails and A10's IoU is ≥ 0.9 in
      ≥ 9 of 10 trials, CU1b builds A10's capture as the image source (`image_fallback=a10`).
      Otherwise the arrow stands (`image_fallback=arrow`), and an issue is filed with A10's
      numbers for the day `currentSystem` answers nil.
    - **The event clock** is the hypothesis whose arrival minus event time lies in [0, 20 ms]
      for ≥ 99 % of events.
    - **Secure input:** delivered keys are noted, and the recorder drops them by
      `IsSecureEventInputEnabled()` either way (CU-7).
  - *Verdict line:*
    `VERDICT positions=<poll|events> clicks=<tap|monitor|STOP> keys=<tap|monitor|STOP> cursor_image=<current-system|none> hidden=<recorded|not-recorded> image_fallback=<a10|arrow> event_clock=<ns|mach|uptime> secure=<withheld|delivered> relaunch=<needed|not-needed>`.
- **CU-S2 — From global points to movie pixels, and the time anchor.** Runs before CU1a.
  - *Question:* which mapping from a polled global position (Quartz points, top-left origin)
    to the movie's pixels is right for each source, and which anchor puts the samples on the
    movie's clock, with the pointer in the picture and with Separate's configuration?
  - *Instrument, In the picture:*
    - It records with `showsCursor = true` over a flat-colour full-screen window of its own.
      The burned cursor's tip is the truth, found per decoded frame by thresholding against
      the flat colour.
    - It warps the cursor along a known path.
    - It logs every frame's `SCStreamFrameInfo` and the polled samples.
  - *Instrument, Separate:* Separate's exact configuration (`showsCursor = false`,
    `showMouseClicks = false`, 420v). The pointer no longer dirties the screen, so the truth
    is a marker of the instrument's own: a 24 pt square in a contrasting colour whose top-left
    corner the instrument moves to the warped point at each step, found per decoded frame. The
    screen therefore changes at every step, as a moving window would.
  - *Still start, Separate:* the instrument holds the screen still for 2 s while the cursor
    moves, then flips a full-screen flat field's colour at a host time it logs. The first
    frame showing the flip gives the movie time of that host time. It records which anchor the
    segment used (E2 or E1) and the anchor's error.
  - *Sources:* a display at Nominal; a display at Best (2×); the instrument's own window, moved
    and then resized during the recording; a window of odd size (1001 × 701 pt at 1×); a
    picked window; a second display when attached (skipped by name otherwise). Each source
    runs in both configurations.
  - *Candidates:*
    - **M1.** `pixel = (p − screenRect.origin) × contentScale × pixelsPerPoint +
      contentRect.origin × pixelsPerPoint`, with pixelsPerPoint = the stream's configured
      pixel width ÷ its point width. An encoder's padding column lies outside the content.
    - **M2.** M1 with `scaleFactor` in place of pixelsPerPoint.
    - **M3.** A fixed display frame from `SCDisplay.frame` (for display sources).
    - Anchors: E2, E1 and `DisplayTime` of the first complete frame.
  - *Rule:*
    - **Mapping.** The first of M1, M2, M3 whose tip error is ≤ 1.5 movie px at the 95th
      percentile on every source row, odd window included, over still frames, wins.
    - **Anchor.** The first of E2, E1 and DisplayTime whose time error is ≤ one frame interval
      at the 95th percentile on every row of BOTH configurations, measured over moving frames
      by the position error divided by the speed there.
    - **Still start.** E1's error over 10 still-start runs is ≤ 25 ms at the 95th percentile
      (#370's 21 ms and a margin). If it is not, the limit is recorded and the file still
      names E1.
    - **STOP.** If no candidate passes for window sources, window recordings keep the cursor
      burned in. The panel greys Separate for Window, and the owner is told. If none passes
      for displays, the bet stops after CU1b. If a candidate passes In the picture and fails
      only Separate, Separate is not the default (CU-36 makes In the picture the default) and
      the owner is told.
- **CU-S3 — Do dirty rects locate typing?** Runs before CU1a, because CU1a's file either
  stores dirty-rect boxes or does not.
  - *Instrument:*
    - It records its own `NSTextView` while text is inserted programmatically, so no key event
      is needed.
    - Distractors run at the same time: the menu-bar clock, a spinner elsewhere, and a playing
      animation in another window.
    - Per burst it takes the median centre of the per-frame dirty-rect bounding boxes, against
      the caret rect the text view reports.
  - *Rule:*
    - **Pass** if within 64 pt of the caret in ≥ 9 of 10 bursts. CU1a's file then stores each
      complete frame's dirty-rect bounding box, and CU7 aims typing zooms at their median
      centre.
    - **Fail** otherwise: nothing about dirty rects is stored, and typing zooms aim at the
      last click before the burst, else the cursor's position at its start.
- **CU-S4 — The file's size and speed.** Runs on synthetic files.
  - *Instrument:* the core's reader prototype over a worst case: one hour of continuous
    movement sampled at 120 Hz (432,000 samples), 3,600 clicks, 20,000 key marks, 40 images.
    Each figure is measured through a JSON request and answer, as `rc_cursor_query` will run
    it.
  - *Rule:*
    - **JSON** (columnar integer microseconds and points ×100) if all three hold:
      - the file is ≤ 25 MB;
      - parse and validate take ≤ 300 ms;
      - `state at t` takes ≤ 20 µs median, request and answer included, once prepared.
    - **Otherwise a binary columnar body** (little-endian i64 arrays after a JSON header),
      version 1 either way.
    - **Smoothing's precompute** (`prepare` at smoothing 1) takes ≤ 1 s on the one-hour file.
      If it does not, smoothing is prepared per 60 s window on demand, still off the
      compositor's thread (CU-37), and the verdict says which.
- **CU-S5 — Motion blur's cost.** Runs before CU11; it may run any time after CU0b.
  - *Instrument:* a probe through `MetalRenderer`'s pipelines draws one full-canvas layer N
    times at sub-frame transforms (a 2× zoom's middle, eased), accumulated in `rgba16Float`,
    for N ∈ {4, 8, 16}, at 1920×1080 and 3840×2160. It measures GPU time per frame against
    the same frame drawn once.
  - *Rule:*
    - **Ship zoom blur** at the largest N in {16, 8, 4} whose added GPU time is ≤ 4 ms at 1080p
      and ≤ 8 ms at 4K on the owner's Mac, in preview and export alike (parity: one N).
    - **STOP zoom blur** if N = 4 misses either bound. The numbers are recorded and an issue is
      filed. Cursor blur, N sprite samples inside `layerSample`, ships either way.

#### CU2 — the core evaluates a cursor file

- **What a person gets:** nothing visible. This is the arithmetic CU3a draws with, and the path
  VR reads.
- **Core:**
  - `cursor_track.rs`: the loaded file. It maps global points to movie pixels (CU-S2's
    mapping, per geometry change), and sample times to source ticks.
  - `cursor_smooth.rs`: smoothing.
    - The path is pinned at every click.
    - It is simplified with a tolerance that grows with `smoothing`, then drawn as a
      centripetal Catmull–Rom spline in time.
    - `smoothing` 0 is the raw samples, linearly interpolated, needing no precompute.
    - It is non-causal, so the smoothed cursor never lags a click.
    - It is computed by a `prepare` request, once per track and smoothing value, and kept in the
      handle under its lock. A `state` request at a smoothing not prepared answers the raw path;
      it never computes one.
  - Idle hide:
    - Hidden after `hide_idle` seconds without movement, with a 0.2 s fade.
    - Shown again 0.15 s BEFORE the next movement.
    - Hidden throughout a recorded `hidden` span.
  - Ripples: each down click's ring phase over 0.45 s.
  - `cursor_query.rs`, the request vocabulary of `rc_cursor_query`:
    - `prepare {smoothing}`;
    - `state {at, props}`: visible; x, y in movie pixels; the image id and its size in movie
      pixels at `scale`; opacity; the active ripples; and, when asked (CU11), the positions at
      the shutter's two ends;
    - `image {id}`: the PNG, base64;
    - `events {from, to, kinds}`: clicks, scrolls, shortcuts and typing stretches;
    - `path {from, to, step, smoothing}`: the smoothed position sampled in source time, at
      most 10 Hz. VR's reframing reads this (named here for VR, which owns its use).

    Later phases add `plan_zooms` (CU7), `plan_overlays` (CU8) and `plan_typing` (CU9b).
  - `core/tests/cursor_track.rs` over hand-written fixture files with known answers.
- **FFI:** `rc_cursor_query(tracks, n, project, request_json, err_out) → char *`, pure. Header
  and the three-file lockstep, within CU1a's room (CU-9).
- **Swift:**
  - `ReelCursor.query` in `ReelCore.swift`; the typed answers in `CursorValues.swift`.
  - `CursorTracks.swift`: a process-wide registry of open tracks keyed by the file's path,
    size and modification second, LRU with a small count.
    - **Loading and preparing happen off main and off the compositor's thread**, on a utility
      queue: `RecipeSource.set` and `Playback.update` ask for each cursor media on the timeline,
      at the smoothing each of its clips uses.
    - The compositor's read, `ready(path:smoothing:)`, never blocks: it answers a prepared track
      or nothing.
    - A landing posts `.cursorTrackDidLand`, so a paused frame redraws.
    - `wait(paths:smoothings:)` is the export's (CU3a).
    - `-RCDevCursorLoadHold <s>` holds each load (dev only), so a proof can act while one is
      pending.
  - No drawing yet.
- **MCP:** none.
- **Docs:** spec §7.1 (the export and its request vocabulary), §7.10 (the modules);
  `core/CLAUDE.md`'s and `app/CLAUDE.md`'s maps.
- **Decisions (draft, CU-20…):**

    down clicks and typing stretches. CU-S3 decides where a typing stretch aims.
    - An anchor within "Stay" of the previous one joins its visit.
    - A scroll burst or a longer gap ends the visit.
  - **Each visit is several actions:**
    - a zoom-in that ends at its first anchor;
    - a pan for each later anchor outside the region's inner 60 %;
    - a pan for the followed cursor that leaves the inner 70 % for more than 0.3 s (at most one

      later clip's source continuing the previous one's: the halves of a split.

    - **The same chord again** before the overlay ends extends it to 1.5 s after the last press,
      and its label becomes "×k" for k presses (the label is otherwise "").
    - **A different chord** pressed sooner: the earlier overlay ends where the later one
      starts. The later one starts at its press, or, when the earlier has not yet had
      D_min(n) frames, at the moment it has. If that delays it more than 0.5 s after its press,

### Risks

- **`NSCursor.currentSystem` will answer nil "in a future version of macOS"** (`NSCursor.h:155`).
  - It typechecks with no warning today (SDK 26.2, target 26.0). A later SDK may mark it
    deprecated at 27.0. That adds a warning to the 4-warning baseline only if Swift warns below
    the deployment target.
  - At run time the recorder checks every sample for nil; a recording with no image draws the
    arrow and says so (CU-S1's rule). CU-S1's A10 measures a replacement, which is built only
    if `currentSystem` already fails.
- **Input Monitoring is attributed to the terminal for a shell launch** (R0 q1), and an event
  tap may need a relaunch after the grant. The sentences carry `launchClause`, CU-S1 measures
  the relaunch, and JOB-4 checks it.
- **Key data is sensitive.** CU-7's mitigations: no typed character is ever stored; nothing
  during secure input; a visible mark. The remaining limit: a password typed where secure input
  is off leaves its keystroke times in the file. The panel's sentence and the guide say so,
  and JOB-5 shows it.
- **Granted proofs.** An ad-hoc build loses Screen Recording, Input Monitoring and the poster's
  Accessibility at every `make app` (CJ-4), so the granted rows skip by name in a pipeline.
  Every mutant listed has an ungranted killer (a probe, `land_recording` or a fixture); the
  granted rows are extra coverage, and their residue is JOB rows.
- **The frame watch is now on every screen recording.** Its resume workaround (CAM-9 (6)) was
  measured in only 2 + 3 runs. K4 runs pause and resume on every granted proof run, K0 holds the
  rule, and K6 bounds its CPU.
- **A cursor file lost or not moved with the movie leaves a Separate recording with no
  pointer.** Mitigations:
  - Consolidate carries it (CU5) and Relink keeps or replaces it (CU3b);
  - the Media tab names a missing file;
  - an export and `render_frame` name it in `cursor_warnings`;
  - In the picture stays available;
  - CU-14 makes a failed write the landing's note.
- **Timing.** E1's fallback (21 ms) is about one 60 fps frame. With Separate it is used
  whenever a segment starts on a still screen; CU-S2 bounds it and K9 checks it.
- **Window sources.** An occluding window over the recorded window still shows the cursor at
  its position, because occlusion is not sampled. CU-S2 may STOP window sources, which then
  keep the burned pointer.
- **Hidden cursors.** An app that hides the pointer while typing may still report an image.
  CU-S1's A9 measures it; if no signal tells, Hide when idle is the remedy and the limit is
  recorded.
- **The render path.** The cursor costs one branch and one sample per tap of the layer stage;
  L7 bounds it at 1080p, 4K and 5K. Loading and smoothing never run on the compositor's thread
  (CU-37).
- **`ReelCore.swift`'s room.** The wrapper is paid for by a doc-only cut; if it grows past the
  room, the phase cuts more docs first (CU1a). A later bet that needs an `rc_*` export meets a
  file with fewer doc lines left to cut.
- **`retime_range` is a wide op.** Its refusals (linked pairs, out-of-range rates, transitions,
  nests, captions) are deliberate, so it never guesses. The trial says whether a refused case
  matters.
- **Generated zooms are subjective.** Creators distrust automatic cuts (survey D16, D17). Every
  zoom is an editable action, Replace is off by default, and CU12's verdict decides the
  defaults.
- **Shared files.** Bets 3 and 6 also touch the layer stage, the recipe, the recorder panel and
  the catalog. The integrator serializes merges in lane B and against lane C.
- **The tool count grows by six**: `get_cursor_events`, `auto_zoom`, `add_shortcut_overlays`
  and `speed_up_typing`, plus the op tools for `set_media_cursor` and `retime_range`. Each
  phase that adds one updates:
  - the catalog snapshot;
  - the assistant's lists;
  - the gate's count;
  - the root CLAUDE.md's "one hundred and six product tools".

### Not in this bet

- Reconstructing a cursor for recordings made before CU3c, or for imported screen videos (no
  vision pass).
- Typed text as overlays (an "all keys" mode). CU-7 says why: it would put whatever was typed
  into the project and every agent's reach.
- Click sounds, cursor packs a person imports, and styles beyond As recorded and Arrow.
- Callouts other than keystrokes: arrows and highlights stay hand-placed graphics.
- Zooms planned from the transcript (bet 1's) and camera layouts (bet 6's, CAM-10 stands here).
- A global hotkey to start or stop a recording. The status item stays the chrome, and Input
  Monitoring is used only for shortcut capture.
- Frame interpolation for sped-up typing. A speed-up drops frames, as `set_speed` does.
- Live auto zoom while recording, and recording an iOS device's screen.

   through one JSON request, keeps the rule, and pays with a named doc-only cut in CU1a (about
   30 lines, ceiling 766); CJ's row is to be corrected.
2. **CU's own lanes.** Accepted. The lanes are gone; CU runs serially in CJ's lane B with its

   inside a nest with no markers to move. Mutants R5, R6, R8.

   (never `region: null` on a later half), keeps transitions off cuts, and CU10 now runs Auto
   Zoom before Speed Up Typing. Rows Z7, Z8.

#### CU7 — Auto Zoom

- **What a person gets:** Clip ▸ Auto Zoom… on one or more clips whose media has cursor data,
  at the top level or inside an open nest.
  - **The sheet:**
    - Zoom (1.25–4×, default 2×);
    - Arrive before the click (default 0.6 s);
    - Stay after the last activity (default 2.5 s);
    - Follow the cursor while zoomed (on);
    - Zoom on typing (on when the file has keys);
    - Replace existing zooms (off).
  - **One undo step, "Auto Zoom".** Every zoom it makes is an ordinary action.
- **Core:**
  - **`cursor_zoom.rs`, the planner** (`plan_zooms` request). Visits are formed from anchors:
    down clicks and typing stretches. CU-S3 decides where a typing stretch aims.
    - An anchor within "Stay" of the previous one joins its visit.
    - A scroll burst or a longer gap ends the visit.
  - **Each visit is several actions:**
    - a zoom-in that ends at its first anchor;
    - a pan for each later anchor outside the region's inner 60 %;
    - a pan for the followed cursor that leaves the inner 70 % for more than 0.3 s (at most one
      pan per second);
    - a zoom back.
  - **Runs and the rest placement (CU-74).**
    - A **run** is adjacent clips on one track, touching, of one media, playing forward, each
      later clip's source continuing the previous one's: the halves of a split.
    - A run's **rest placement** is its first clip's base `scale`, `x`, `y`.
    - Every zoom back ends at the rest placement, explicitly: `region: null` when the clip's
      base equals it, else the region whose solve gives it (`edit_zoom.rs` gains the inverse of
      (★) for a placement). A later half that starts zoomed is never zoomed "back" to its own
      base.
    - Visits are planned over the run, in run time. A zoom-in, pan or zoom-back never straddles
      a cut: one that would is moved to end at the cut (in) or to start at it (pan, back). A
      hold that crosses a cut sets the later clip's base to the visit's placement
      (`set_video {scale, x, y}`); if that clip has a kept action in the hold, the visit is
      closed at the cut instead, and the change is counted.
    - With Replace, each later clip of a run whose base is not the rest placement and that no
      kept action moves is reset to it.
  - **A placed clip is refused (CU-75).** A clip whose rest placement is smaller than the
    media's fit (`edit_fit.rs`'s `fit_scale`, by more than 0.1 %) or off the canvas centre by
    more than 1 px — a CO layout's, a picture in picture — is refused by name: "clip C is
    placed on the canvas; a zoom would fill the canvas. Nest it (Clip ▸ Nest) and run Auto
    Zoom inside the nest." Inside an open nest the zoom fills the nest's canvas, which the
    layout then places (CO-62's direction, reversed).
  - **A reversed clip is refused** by name (CU-5).
  - **Region and timing:**
    - The region has the canvas's aspect at the chosen zoom and is clamped inside the source.
    - Visits whose zoom-back would end within 1 s of the next zoom-in merge into a pan.
    - Times are mapped through the clip's source map.
    - Actions are clamped inside the clip.
    - Overlap with an existing action drops the planned action, which is counted.
  - **`cursor_bursts.rs`:** typing stretches (marks less than 1.0 s apart, at least 3 marks).
    This is shared with CU9b.
  - **`action_is_zoom`:** the core's twin of `ActionBands.isZoom`.
  - **The plan** is answered as `remove_action` ops (Replace only), `set_video` ops (a run's
    later bases), then `add_zoom_action` ops.
- **FFI:** none new: `plan_zooms {clips, settings}` through `rc_cursor_query`, one track per
  clip (CU-9).
- **Swift:**
  - `AutoZoomSheetController.swift`.
  - `EditorViewController+AutoZoom.swift` with its validator arm (enabled when every selected
    clip's media has cursor data), passing the open nest's scope.
  - The menu item in `AppDelegate+ClipMenus.swift` (153).
  - The edit through `performGroupedEdit`.
- **MCP:** `auto_zoom {clip | clips, zoom?, lead?, stay?, follow?, typing?, replace?, from?,

- **Docs:** `screen-recording.md` ("Auto Zoom"), `motion-and-transitions.md` (zoom actions),

  - `cursor_overlays.rs` (`plan_overlays` request): shortcut times mapped to project time through
    each clip's window and source map; reversed clips refused (CU-5).
  - **Timing (CU-80).** The template's own timing sets the floor. With n the chord's keycaps and
    the canvas rate's frames, its last keycap presses at frame 5n + 14 (`pressAt`,
    `keyboard-keys.js:93`) and it exits over the clip's last 15 frames (:94), so a clip shorter
    than **D_min(n) = 5n + 30 frames** cuts the press or the exit.

    - **The same chord again** before the overlay ends extends it to 1.5 s after the last press,
      and its label becomes "×k" for k presses (the label is otherwise "").
    - **A different chord** pressed sooner: the earlier overlay ends where the later one
      starts. The later one starts at its press, or, when the earlier has not yet had
      D_min(n) frames, at the moment it has. If that delays it more than 0.5 s after its press,
      it is dropped and counted ("N shortcuts came too close to show").

#### CU9a — retime a range

- **What a person gets:** Clip ▸ Retime Range… (beside Close Gap) speeds up or slows down the

  - **`edit_retime.rs`, `retime_range {from, to, rate, keep_pitch?}`.**
    - Every clip on an unlocked track that `from` or `to` is strictly inside is split there,
      by `split`'s rules.
    - Each media clip in [from, to) plays at its rate × `rate` (`set_speed`'s arm, actions
      keeping their fraction, a ramped clip by SR-19's factor). Its start becomes
      from + (start − from) / rate, snapped so that touching clips still touch.

      the same way. A graphic keeps its `length` (G-9), so it shows the part of its animation
      its new duration covers.
    - Markers inside scale. Clips and markers at or after `to` move earlier by the range's
      lost length, each moved clip's linked partner with it (AU-91's shift).
    - **Inside a nest** it applies to the nest's tracks. A nest's view has no markers, so none
      move (`scope.rs`). It is not in `refused_inside`.

    - a timed caption page in it (a rate-change re-time is SR-27's, app side);
    - a locked track holding a clip at or after `from`;
    - a range under two frames;
    - a `rate` past ×0.1–×1000.
